title: About
text: I am a mixed-methods social sciences researcher and educator whose work critically advances the understanding of nationalism, ethnic conflict, and imperialism. My contributions intersect three core areas: the re-examination of nationalism as a transformative and often contingent phenomenon; the integration of innovative methodologies—including Geographic Information System (GIS) tools and advanced quantitative techniques—into sociological and historical analysis; and theoretical advancements that challenge and refine dominant frameworks in sociology and related disciplines. My research engages with pressing debates on the legacies of imperialism, the role of historical education systems in shaping identity, and the mechanisms by which conflict and transformation affect socio-political cohesion.

title: Teaching
text:
Nationalism and Ethnic Conflict


Fall 2021
Instructor for a master-level elective course. The course focuses on the rise and resilience of nationalism, its role in conflict and war, but also in other fields, including economic development and public goods provision.

title: Teaching
text:
Education and Inequality


January 2020
Substitute instructor for a 200-level introductory course on sociology. The course focuses on the mechanisms by which educational institutions foster and maintain equalities and inequalities around the world.

title: Teaching
text:
Sociological Perspectives


Summer 2019, Fall 2021
Instructor for a 200-level introductory course on sociology. The course introduced students to a wide range of topics including (but not limited to) social inequality and social class, race and ethnicity, gender, deviance and social movements.
